newsitem.title: UKRAINE: UKRAINE TO HALT STATE GRAIN ORDERS NEXT YEAR.
newsitem.headline: UKRAINE TO HALT STATE GRAIN ORDERS NEXT YEAR.

text.p: Ukraine plans next year to stop its Soviet-era practice of government purchases of set amounts of domestic grain and replace it with a fund for producers to buy machinery, Agriculture Minister Yuri Karasyk said on Thursday.
"We will not have state orders next year," Karasyk told his first news conference since being appointed late last month.
"We would use the funds to create a leasing fund for producers to get long-term credits they can use to buy machinery," he said. "We have to buy combines for 1998."
This year's state order is 5.88 million tonnes against 5.00 million tonnes last year. Ukraine has forecast a total grain harvest of 37-38 million tonnes this year against 25.4 million tonnes in 1996.
Western experts doubt that Ukraine, independent for six years, can do away with state orders for a sector heavily dependent on state money to buy machinery, fertilisers and fuel.
The government set state-order grain prices, effective August 1, at $247.20 for first-class wheat and $98.90 for fifth-class wheat.
